title: Enterprise Contract Governance and Billing Acceptance Playbook
author: Sofia Morales
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the cross-functional governance steps and minimum acceptance criteria required to move an executed enterprise contract into production billing and revenue recognition. It aligns Legal, Finance, Sales, Procurement and Engineering (Billing/Platform) on a single, auditable path from contract signature to billing enablement. The goal is to eliminate handoff ambiguity, reduce time-to-bill, and ensure revenue recognition controls (SOX-friendly) are satisfied.

Scope:
- Applies to all enterprise customer contracts and amendments that will be invoiced via Redwood billing systems (hosted API subscriptions, Dedicated commitments, customer private deployments add-ons).
- Covers commercial terms ingestion, contract metadata standards, billing acceptance checks, revrec triggers, procurement handoffs for CAPEX/OPEX requests, and exception handling.
- Excludes routine self-serve subscriptions that are covered by standard billing automation.

Owners and stakeholders:
- Document owner: Finance (Sofia Morales)
- Legal owner: ContractOps (Liam Chen)
- Billing/Platform: Revenue Engineering (Marcus Lee)
- Sales/Account: Account Executive / Sales Operations (named AE)
- Procurement: Procurement Ops (Priya Nair)

Key definitions:
- Billing Enablement: The point at which the Billing Service (revrec-api) is configured to issue invoices for the customer and usage is billable.
- RevRec Trigger Event: The specific contractual milestone that starts revenue recognition (e.g., service delivery, shipment, SaaS activation date, or pro-rated subscription start).
- Contract Canonical Record (CCR): Single source of truth record in ContractOps (contract-id) that contains required contract metadata.

Minimum contract metadata (Contract Canonical Record)
The following fields MUST be captured in the CCR before billing enablement. Missing fields are a gating issue. Each field maps to the internal Billing Service and RevRec pipeline.

| Field name | Required | Example | Notes |
|------------|----------|---------|-------|
| contract_id | yes | CT-2026-1345 | UUID generated by ContractOps upon countersignature |
| customer_id | yes | cust_0a1b2c | Redwood customer PK |
| billing_entity | yes | Redwood Inc (US) | Legal entity responsible for invoicing |
| currency | yes | USD | 3-letter ISO |
| sku_list | yes | hosted-api-monthly,dedicated-reserve | Comma-separated SKUs mapped to pricebook |
| contract_start | yes | 2026-03-15 | date (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| billing_start | yes | 2026-03-15 | date - when invoices begin |
| revrec_trigger | yes | SaaS_activation | enum: SaaS_activation, Shipment, Milestone |
| payment_terms | yes | Net 30 | used by AR and dunning |
| auto_renew | no | true | boolean |
| termination_fee | no | 50000 | currency amount |

Minimum billing acceptance checks (pre-boarding checklist)
1) Contract record completeness: CCR fields present and validated.
2) Pricebook mapping: All SKUs in contract have mapped pricebook entries in Pricebook Service (pricebook-v2).
3) Entity & tax: Billing entity and tax configuration verified; VAT/Tax ID validated for non-US customers.
4) Payment instrument: Payment method on file (if required by Sales) or AR onboarding complete for invoiced customers.
5) Start/End dates and proration rules: Confirm billing_start, contract_start, and any trial or grace periods.
6) RevRec alignment: Revrec_trigger confirmed by Finance with revrec policy (see "Revenue Recognition Routing" below).
7) System access: Billing Service (revrec-api), ContractOps, and Customer Portal accounts verified for the AE and Billing Onboarding owner.
8) Compliance flags: Check confidentiality/data residency flags; if restricted, follow Private Deployment billing route.

Step-by-step: Contract to Billing Enablement (recommended sequence)
1. Sales executes contract and uploads final countersigned PDF to ContractOps. (owner: AE)
2. ContractOps creates CCR and populates required metadata; runs automated validation rules. (owner: ContractOps)
3. Legal reviews and approves any non-standard clauses; signs off in ContractOps (owner: Legal).
4. Finance performs pricing review and confirms SKU mappings & revrec_trigger. (owner: Finance Revenue Ops)
5. Procurement (if customer requires purchase order or if Redwood needs to raise PO for third-party procurement) completes procurement handoffs. (owner: Procurement)
6. Billing/Platform receives CCR and performs system-side mapping to pricebook-v2 and sets up billing_entity. (owner: Revenue Engineering)
7. Billing acceptance checklist executed. If all checks pass, Billing Service flagged as ENABLED for customer. (owner: Revenue Engineering)
8. First invoice scheduled per payment_terms and billing_start. (owner: AR)

Sample CCR payload (YAML example)
```yaml
contract_id: CT-2026-1345
customer_id: cust_0a1b2c
billing_entity: "Redwood Inference, Inc"
currency: USD
sku_list:
  - hosted-api-monthly: 1
  - dedicated-reserve: 2
contract_start: 2026-03-15
billing_start: 2026-03-15
revrec_trigger: SaaS_activation
payment_terms: Net 30
auto_renew: true
```

Revenue recognition routing (high level)
- SaaS_activation: Recognize revenue over the service period from billing_start to contract_end on a straight-line basis unless a milestone schedule exists.
- Shipment/delivery: Recognize when goods are delivered and customer acceptance criteria are met.
- Milestone: Recognize upon objective milestones; Finance must record milestone schedule and linkage in RevRec ledger.

Examples of gating and approval thresholds
- Any contract with total contract value (TCV) >= $1,000,000 requires Director of Finance approval for revrec_trigger and billing_start.
- Any non-standard payment_terms (e.g., Net 90) require Legal + Finance sign-off.
- Contracts with revenue deferral > 12 months require VP Finance review.

Procurement & CAPEX handoff (when applicable)
- If the customer's contract requires Redwood to procure specific hardware or dedicated capacity on the customer's behalf, Procurement must produce a Purchase Order (PO) and SOW. The PO number must be noted in CCR.purchase_order.
- For on-prem/private deployments, infrastructure installation acceptance is a separate milestone; Billing Enablement for the managed services portion may be staged only after installation acceptance.

Escalation and exception handling
- If CCR validation fails, ContractOps creates a "Contract Block" and assigns a remediation ticket to the AE and ContractOps. Block reasons are recorded in the CCR (e.g., pricebook_missing, tax_mismatch, missing_payment_instrument).
- If billing_enablement is delayed > 10 business days after countersignature, an escalation to Director, Revenue Ops is triggered automatically.
- For disputes about revrec_trigger or revenue timing, raise a "RevRec Dispute" in the RevRec Issue Tracker (link: /revrec-issues) with Finance, Legal, and Revenue Engineering copied.

Audit & controls
- Every change to CCR must be auditable. ContractOps maintains an immutable activity log with user, timestamp, and change reason.
- Monthly sampling: Finance will sample 10% of newly enabled accounts each month to confirm contract to system mapping and revrec treatment. Findings must be remediated within the same quarter.

Operational playbook: common scenarios
A) Amendment that increases TCV but does not change billing_start
1. AE uploads amendment PDF and selects "amendment" in ContractOps.
2. ContractOps validates delta SKU mappings and TCV.
3. Finance confirms pricing and determines whether a change in revrec schedule is required.
4. Billing Service applies delta invoices starting on the agreed date.

B) Customer requests delayed billing start (retroactive activation)
- Requires written approval from Director, Revenue Ops and update to CCR with justification. Retroactive billing cannot be more than 90 days prior to approval date without VP Finance approval.

C) Early termination with termination fee
- ContractOps records termination_fee in CCR. AR will issue final invoice for outstanding amounts plus termination fee in the next invoice cycle. Finance will evaluate revrec implications and reverse deferred revenue where applicable.

Metrics and SLA targets for billing enablement
- Target time from countersignature to billing-enabled: 5 business days (SLA).
- Escalation threshold: >10 business days -> Director, Revenue Ops notified.
- Billing error rate (post-enable invoices requiring correction): <0.5% of invoices in a 30-day rolling window.

Related tools and services
- ContractOps: Contract canonicalization and activity log (owner: Legal)
- Pricebook-v2: Central pricebook service mapping SKUs to catalog prices (owner: Product Finance)
- Revrec-api / Billing Service: Invoice orchestration, taxation, and AR handoffs (owner: Revenue Engineering)
- ProcureFlow: Procurement tracking & POs (owner: Procurement)

Change log
- 2025-10-12: Initial published version (Sofia Morales).
- 2026-02-28: Clarified revrec_trigger enum and added procurement CAPEX handoff (reviewers: Liam Chen, Priya Nair).

Appendix: Quick remediation checklist for common CCR failures
- pricebook_missing: Request Pricebook-v2 mapping; temporary charge hold until mapping complete.
- tax_mismatch: Engage TaxOps for VAT/TIN verification; hold invoices until resolved.
- missing_payment_instrument: AE to collect payment details or AR to confirm invoicing cadence.
